office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_numbering: The markers are the numbers Word shows, not a repeated '1.'. CommonMark takes a list's start from its FIRST marker and counts up on its own, so writing '1.' on every item was only correct while nothing ever split the list; the nested step is 2.1, so its own marker is 1 and the step after it is 3.
office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_emphasis: The source bolds only the second half of the identifier (a plain run 'Dma' followed by a bold run 'ArbiterUnit'), which is how Word actually stores partial-word formatting. Faithful output is therefore 'Dma**ArbiterUnit**'. The tradeoff is deliberate and recorded in docs/quality-plan.md: the emphasis is real information the document carries, and markdown_to_text strips the markers before tokenizing, so the identifier is intact in the text layer the index and the KB consume. What is lost is a raw grep of document.md for the unsplit identifier.

office/kestrel-reordered.pptx._note: The deck's p:sldIdLst says 1,5,3,4,2 and its slide PARTS are unrenumbered -- what PowerPoint writes every time a user drags a slide. Sorting part names therefore publishes the order the slides were DRAFTED in. The TOKEN gate cannot see that -- it compares multisets, so the wrong order and the right one both measure recall 1.0 / n_source 135 -- and until P9.6 nothing else could either. Now structure_fidelity grades it: injecting the exact bug (the slide order read off the unqualified id attribute) moves block_sequence, heading_path and list_item_words, and the gate fails while recall stays at 1.0. The heading pins below are the second, human-readable half of that check.

legacy/kestrel-registers.xls._note: Also flipped by P9.4, and the reach of the pass is narrower than it looks. Both halves of the gate read the package LibreOffice produced, so anything the pre-convert already destroyed is destroyed in the source the ground truth reads and the truth agrees with it. `pass` here means 'faithful from the converted package onward', never 'nothing was lost' -- which is why report.json declares blind_to: pre_conversion_structure on this lane. Measured cost of that round trip on this document: the boolean Gated column arrives as 1/0 instead of TRUE/FALSE and Scale loses its 1.0 notation.

legacy/kestrel-overview.ppt._note: The LibreOffice lane's honest caveat, pinned. Both halves of the structure gate read the package soffice PRODUCED, so whatever the round trip already destroyed is destroyed in the ground truth too and the truth agrees with it: measured, soffice writes NO p:ph declarations at all, so every slide title is demoted to a body bullet and every outline level flattened to 0 -- and the gate passes over it. `pass` here means 'faithful from the converted package onward', never 'nothing was lost', which is why the report carries pre_conversion_structure in blind_to.

pdf/kestrel-clock-spec.pdf._note_fidelity: unmeasured, not best-effort: there is no second implementation that can read structure out of a PDF, so nothing was graded and the block says so. best-effort would imply a measurement was taken on a best-effort basis.
